delta.name: Delta
delta.why: The name is a fossil. This glass box rides the fifth floor of the Greek National Opera, above a Renzo Piano park laid over the silted-up Faliro delta where the Kifissos river once met the sea. Two chefs opened it in 2022 — Thanos Feskos, in from Copenhagen's Geranium, and Giorgos Papazacharias, in from Oslo's Maaemo — cooking small Greek producers through Nordic-trained technique. Feskos left in early 2025 to open his own house; Papazacharias kept the pass alone. You clear SNFCC security, ride up past the opera, and the room hands you the Saronic light before the first course lands.
delta.verdict: The only two-MICHELIN-star kitchen in Greece — and the 2026 Athinorama jury still ranked the solo Papazacharias kitchen joint-second in the country.
delta.signature: Twelve-course Omnivore menu: Greek terroir driven vegetal and precise, the Saronic light on the glass.
delta.caveat: Not for a casual night out — a deposit-backed, full-evening gastronomic performance, not dinner.
delta.person: Giorgos Papazacharias, head chef — ex-Maaemo (Oslo) and creator of the 'Under' menu; co-won Greece's first two stars in 2022, then held them alone after Feskos left in 2025.

spondi.name: Spondi
spondi.neighborhood: Pangrati · quiet street behind Varnava Square
spondi.why: Spondi opened in 1996 and taught Athens what two Michelin stars felt like — it wore them for years before the Guide trimmed it back to one. The pass now belongs to Arnaud Bignon, a Frenchman who earned two stars of his own at London's The Greenhouse, working with head chef Manolis Demetzos. Thirty years on, the cooking is still unrepentantly French-school — classical architecture, Aegean ingredients, a whisper of Asia — and a cheese trolley is wheeled to the table, which almost no one else in this city still does. In summer it all happens in a stone courtyard under bougainvillea, behind Varnava Square where Pangrati goes quiet.
spondi.verdict: Still the most technically exacting French kitchen in Greece — a one-star room that plates like the two-star it used to be.
spondi.signature: Signature tasting menu: classical French architecture over Aegean ingredients, three decades of polish, an Asian inflection.
spondi.caveat: Not for seekers of 'modern Greek' — this is unapologetically French-school fine dining, jacket-comfortable.
spondi.person: Arnaud Bignon, executive chef — won two MICHELIN stars at London's The Greenhouse before taking Spondi's pass; runs it with head chef Manolis Demetzos.

soil.name: Soil
soil.neighborhood: Pangrati · Ferekydou, behind the Panathenaic Stadium
soil.why: Tasos Mantis came up at Hytra — the kitchen that seeded most of Athens' current starred chefs — then built the city's benchmark farm-driven room inside a restored 1925 townhouse behind the Panathenaic Stadium. Much of what lands on the plate is grown on his own plot at Alepochori, west of the city: fermented vegetables, wild herbs, Greek grains, fire kept quiet, and none of the caviar-and-lobster crutches a starred room usually leans on. In January 2026 Mantis and the Soil team opened a second act, Amphibian, at the Onassis Stegi — but this house, the one that earned the Green Star, keeps cooking.
soil.verdict: The most convincing farm-to-table statement in Athens — a Green Star that actually tastes like one.
soil.signature: Seasonal tasting menu: ferments, wild herbs and heirloom vegetables treated with protein-level respect, quiet fire.
soil.caveat: Not for diners who measure fine dining in caviar and lobster — the garden dictates the plate.
soil.person: Tasos Mantis, chef-patron — the ex-Hytra chef who built Athens' defining farm-driven room; in Jan 2026 returned to the Onassis Stegi with his second act, Amphibian.

gb-roof-garden.name: GB Roof Garden
gb-roof-garden.why: The Grande Bretagne has stood on Syntagma for about 150 years, and its eighth-floor terrace gives you Parliament directly below and the floodlit Acropolis dead ahead, the bar in mid-ritual as the light goes. The kitchen runs under executive chef Asterios Koustoudis — the same hand behind the Michelin star at Tudor Hall, in the group's King George hotel next door — with Giannis Rokanas newly on the pass as chef de cuisine since early 2026. It holds a Michelin Plate, not a star, and a long-running Wine Spectator award for the cellar. Sit at the bar and you skip the dinner commitment entirely.

gb-roof-garden.verdict: The rooftop every Athens rooftop is measured against — 150 years of grand hotel below, the Acropolis full-frontal ahead.

tags: Late, when the fire hits cruising speed
vezene.why: Aris Vezenes has run this room behind the Hilton since 2011, and he sources like a man with a grudge — the dry-aged beef off his wood fire is what every other Athens grill quietly copies. It is a bistro, not a tasting-menu house: whole Aegean fish laid over the same fire and treated with steakhouse seriousness, a cellar serious enough for Star Wine List recognition, and a house dessert, 'Ari's Deal Closer', with its own small cult. The room runs on swagger rather than ceremony, which is exactly why the city's own chefs book it on the night they cook for no one.
vezene.verdict: The chefs' choice for a night off — Athens' best wood-fire cooking, no tasting-menu ceremony attached.

vezene.caveat: Not budget, and not vegetarian-friendly at heart — this is a fire-and-meat room.

mavros-gatos.name: Mavros Gatos
mavros-gatos.why: A few steps down from Polemonos, in a half-basement near Proskopon Square, the checked tablecloths and formica have not moved in decades. The order writes itself: paidakia off the charcoal, a coarse leek sausage, lamb's liver flashed with lemon, cold retsina to cut the fat. LiFO counts the lamb chops among the finest in Athens. Chef Manolis Papoutsakis, of Pharaoh, calls ribs-and-retsina here 'an Athenian staple' — the kind of sentence a working chef only spends on a room he actually returns to. Around EUR 15–20 a head without wine; the smoke gets into your jacket, and that is the point.
mavros-gatos.verdict: Two of Athens' sharpest palates — Papoutsakis and LiFO — send you here for lamb chops, and the basement delivers on both counts.
mavros-gatos.signature: Paidakia: char-crusted thin lamb chops, eaten by hand with cold resinous retsina.
mavros-gatos.caveat: Not for terrace romantics or the offal-shy — meat, charcoal smoke and old-taverna formica, nothing softened.

tags: Book — peak waits; rooftop tables go first

karamanlidika-tou-fani.why: The name honours the Karamanlides — Turkish-speaking Orthodox Christians of Cappadocia who printed Greek in Ottoman script and came west in the 1923 exchange. Fanis Theodoropoulos, a second-generation charcutier who kept shop on Evripidou's old pastourma row, opened this deli-meze in spring 2014 with pastirma-maker Paraskevas Sarimpoyias of Sary, in Drama. Half the restored neoclassical is a counter of cured meat, half a table; the front vacuum-packs pastourma and soutzouki that survive a week in a galley fridge. It deliberately revives the interwar pastourmatzidika, where refugee curers first taught Athens the smell of fenugreek.
karamanlidika-tou-fani.verdict: The pastourma pie and the deli counter alone justify crossing town; everything past the cured-meat canon is merely good.
karamanlidika-tou-fani.signature: Pastourma pie: fenugreek-crusted cured beef and molten cheese in crackling hot phyllo
karamanlidika-tou-fani.caveat: Not for vegetarians or the cumin-averse, and dark on Sundays.
karamanlidika-tou-fani.person: Fanis Theodoropoulos — second-generation charcutier from Evripidou's pastourma row; opened the deli-meze in spring 2014 with pastirma-maker Paraskevas Sarimpoyias of Sary, Drama.

tags: Deli — pay by weight; counter tasting plates

miran.why: Miran Kourounlian, an Armenian refugee from Caesarea — Kayseri, in Cappadocia — fled via Constantinople and Chios and landed in Piraeus, where in 1922 he began salting beef into pastourma; the narrow Evripidou shop followed. Interwar Athenians, hit by the tsimeni's strange perfume of cumin and fenugreek, swore the cured meat was camel. Four generations on, his grandsons Miran and Krikor still cure on the same spice street, their father Berdos having industrialised production in 1983. It is a shop, not a taverna — a renovated counter with a tasting corner where charcuterie boards come with tsipouro amid the market's noise.
miran.hours: Shop hours; closed Sun — call ahead
miran.verdict: No shop in Athens sells better pastourma, and the standing counter-tasting outclasses most sit-down meze in the quarter.

miran.caveat: Not a restaurant — no full meals, no evening hours, strictly carnivore territory.
miran.person: Miran and Krikor Kourounlian — grandsons of founder Miran, an Armenian refugee from Kayseri who began curing pastourma in Piraeus in 1922; father Berdos industrialised it in 1983.

peran-kafe-aman.name: Peran, to Kafe Aman
peran-kafe-aman.neighborhood: Nea Chalkidona · Dekeleias, northern refugee belt
tags: Fri/Sat night for sets; Sun afternoon for lunch
peran-kafe-aman.why: Named for Pera, the European quarter of Constantinople, and set in Nea Chalkidona — a suburb the refugees named for Chalcedon across the Bosphorus. It revives the cafe aman: the improvised-song coffeehouse the uprooted of 1922 carried west, where a singer throws out a line and the room answers 'aman, aman'. Appetisers are chosen off a passing tray, Constantinople-style; the bread and the syrup sweets are baked in the stone-walled room. Wednesday to Saturday it fills for the live sets, Sunday afternoon for a long Politiki family lunch.
peran-kafe-aman.verdict: The last politiki-kouzina table standing in Athinorama's guide, and the live cafe-aman nights alone justify crossing the refugee belt.
peran-kafe-aman.signature: Yogurt kebab with cumin: juicy, gently spicy, bleeding into the house-baked bread
peran-kafe-aman.caveat: Not a quick stop — music nights run long and loud, and it's closed Monday to Wednesday lunch.

diporto.name: Diporto
diporto.why: Two doors, two stairs, one cellar with no sign and no menu: a surviving 1913 lease already calls it a wine shop at 55 drachmas a month. Dimitris Koliolis — kyr-Mitsos — has worked the barrels and pots since 1958, and you eat whatever he decided at dawn, off paper-covered tables shared with market porters. The poet Kostas Varnalis drank and wrote here; clippings of his verses still yellow on the walls. In March 2024 Koliolis said the building had been sold to foreign investors with a year or two to leave; the family co-owner denied it. The pots keep going, exactly as since 1958.
diporto.verdict: There is no older or truer lunch in Athens: a 1913-lease wine cellar where the menu is whatever kyr-Mitsos decided at dawn.
diporto.signature: Revithada: peppery chickpeas ladled straight from the pot, oil-slicked, bread-mopping hot
diporto.caveat: Not for anyone needing a menu, a card machine, a clean floor plan or their own table — and maybe not here in two years.
diporto.person: Dimitris Koliolis, 'kyr-Mitsos' — at the barrels and pots since 1958; in 2024 he told the press the building had been sold under him, and kept cooking.

klimataria.name: Klimataria
klimataria.neighborhood: Plateia Theatrou · on the square, under the vine
tags: Fri/Sat ~22:30; Sunday lunch for the pots
klimataria.why: Open since 1927 on the square that gave it its name, with wine barrels for a back wall and the namesake vine overhead. House lore — and the Greek Gastronomy Guide — holds that the great interwar rebetes passed through when this quarter was the city's working heart, Markos Vamvakaris among them, the Syros coal-lugger who formed Piraeus's Famous Quartet in 1934. A century on the formula is untouched: mageirefta cooked by hand, musicians playing from memory, no amplifier worship, palms keeping the zeibekiko's time. Wednesday to Saturday the compania warms up around 22:30; Sunday belongs to the pots.
klimataria.verdict: The last taverna in central Athens where barrel wine, hand-cooked mageirefta and live rebetes still share one 1927 room several nights a week.
klimataria.signature: Lamb kotsi melomeno: honey-glazed shank collapsing off the bone into its own juices
klimataria.caveat: Not a quiet dinner on music nights — after 22:00 conversation surrenders to the band; on off-nights you find only the kitchen.

taverna-tou-oikonomou.name: Taverna tou Oikonomou
taverna-tou-oikonomou.neighborhood: Ano Petralona · Troon & Kydantidon, opposite Zefyros cinema
tags: Book weekends — pavement tables go first
Summer evening outside, Zefyros flickering opposite
taverna-tou-oikonomou.why: Giorgos Oikonomou opened a butcher's shop with a single cooking pot in 1930; his son Nikos took over in 1950, and the counter only fully surrendered to the dining room in the early 1970s. When two young owners took the keys in 2023, their first public promise was that nothing change — 'neither the environment nor the food' — so Garoufallia, twenty-five years the cook, and her recipes stayed, along with the old tables and the wall paintings. It is a mageireio: the day's pots run out and service ends. Across the lane flickers Zefyros, one of Athens's oldest open-air cinemas.
taverna-tou-oikonomou.verdict: The 1930 butcher's-taverna where Athens still measures what home-stewed rooster and hilopites should taste like.
taverna-tou-oikonomou.signature: Rooster with hilopites: wine-dark bird over egg noodles drinking the slow-cooked sauce
taverna-tou-oikonomou.caveat: Not for grill-seekers or late arrivals — the glory is in the pots, and the pots empty.
taverna-tou-oikonomou.person: Garoufallia — the cook, twenty-five years in this kitchen; when the taverna changed hands in 2023 the new owners' first decision was that she and her recipes stay.

akra.name: Akra
akra.neighborhood: Pangrati · Amynta St, near Proskopon Square
tags: Late dinner, fire in full swing
akra.why: Akra opened in 2023 near Proskopon Square and quickly became the room new Pangrati orbits. A charcoal fire burns continuously; Giannis Loukakis, out of Mourga, cooks whatever the market gave that morning over it, and the menu is rewritten daily around it. The signature at the door is not a grill but a bakery — Spyros Pediaditakis runs an in-house pastry and cake counter you pass on the way in. Michelin made it a Bib Gourmand in the 2024 Greece selection. Loud, convivial, half-portions on offer; walk-ins wait at peak. It reads as a neighbourhood joint and cooks like a serious kitchen.
akra.verdict: The Bib that defines new Pangrati — a daily-changing live-fire kitchen with a working bakery at its own front door.
akra.signature: Daily fire-cooked market dish: the morning's best haul, seared over the continuously burning charcoal.
akra.caveat: Not for vegetarians or quiet-dinner seekers — it is loud, meat-forward and fire-led.
akra.person: Giannis Loukakis (ex-Mourga) leads the live-fire kitchen; Spyros Pediaditakis runs the in-house bakery and pastry at the entrance.

pharaoh.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh.why: Manolis Papoutsakis — the Cretan chef behind Thessaloniki's Charoupi — cooks on Solomou with no electricity or gas in the kitchen at all: wood stoves, charcoal, a wood-fired oven, and a blackboard rewritten almost nightly around the market. Restaurant, bar and wine shop share one room, and the list runs natural-wine-first, more than four hundred labels along the wall. Michelin named it a Bib Gourmand in the 2024 Greece selection, alongside Akra. Regional Greek recipes — island and mountain — come back respectfully updated, lamb and pulses and greens, whatever the day decided. The wine you drink you can carry out the door.
pharaoh.verdict: Athens' best argument that tradition, a wood oven and natural wine make a modern restaurant — and we would cross town for the blackboard.
pharaoh.signature: Wood-oven daily roast: an island or mountain recipe the blackboard picked that morning, slow-cooked in a kitchen with no gas.
pharaoh.caveat: Menu control-freaks beware — you eat what the day decided, not what you planned.
pharaoh.person: Manolis Papoutsakis, chef — revisits Greek regional tradition with a contemporary hand and a daily-changing menu, in a kitchen that runs on no electricity or gas.
